subject: Computer Networking
title: SSH: Secure Remote Access
description: A short lesson to help you apply SSH: Secure Remote Access.

hook.text: A developer in Paris manages a server in Tokyo. They type commands as if sitting right next to it. That's SSH.

buildup.text: SSH encrypts the entire session — login, commands, output. Nobody in between can see what you're doing.

discovery.text: It replaced Telnet, which sent everything in plain text. SSH made remote administration safe.

twist.text: SSH isn't just for terminals. It tunnels other protocols, transfers files via SCP, and powers Git over SSH.

climax.text: Key-based authentication lets you log in without typing a password — more secure and more convenient.

punchline.text: SSH is your encrypted window into a remote machine.

quiz.question: What did SSH replace?
options: Telnet, which sent data in plain text
HTTP, which was too slow for remote access

details.summary: SSH provides encrypted remote access to servers and network devices, replacing insecure protocols like Telnet. It authenticates using passwords or cryptographic key pairs and creates an encrypted tunnel for all commands and data. SSH also supports secure file transfer and port forwarding.
details.whyItMatters: SSH is the standard way to manage servers and network infrastructure remotely. Every system administrator and developer relies on SSH daily for secure command-line access.
takeaways: SSH encrypts all traffic between client and remote server
Key-based authentication is more secure than password login
SSH tunneling forwards ports securely through encrypted connections

faq.question: How do SSH keys work?
faq.answer: You generate a key pair: a private key kept secret on your machine and a public key placed on the server. When connecting, the server challenges you with a puzzle only your private key can solve. This proves identity without transmitting a password. Keys can also be protected with a passphrase.

faq.question: What is SSH port forwarding?
faq.answer: SSH tunneling forwards a local port through the encrypted SSH connection to a remote destination. This lets you securely access services like databases behind firewalls. Local forwarding brings remote services to your machine; remote forwarding exposes local services to the remote network.
